title: Lou Hurd's new band and the 1961 contract for England
summary: After quitting, Polites rejoined when an English trombonist formed a band, and an English agent offered a contract in 1961.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: No. Yeah. Well, uh, so then when you left Frank Johnson, did you go immediately to another band or?

No, I thought that, uh, oh, well, no one's, uh, playing much, uh, worthwhile jazz now, so, uh, that's it. And, uh, um, I just didn't think that, uh, it'd be worth, uh, playing. Um, but a few months later, um, uh, a chap from England, uh, a trombone player called Lou Hurd, um, told me that, uh, he wanted to try and start a band. And, um, so collected a few chaps. They're not very good players, but, uh, were very keen. And, uh, it's the old story. Um, technique doesn't matter that much. And stuff like stuff stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff stuff like stuff stuff Lyn Dutton, the agent in England, heard some of these records and offered us this contract in 1961. So we went over to England and that's where we've been since then.
